identity.name: Far-U / logarithmic-derivative dual
identity.formula: sum_rho 1/(s-rho) = -zeta'/zeta(s) - (trivial zeros contrib) + archimedean (partial fraction of xi); far piece = full - near - trivial - arch
identity.U_model: U ~ 1/((s-rho') log X) so sum_far U ~ (1/log X) * sum_far 1/(s-rho')
identity.standing: classical identity surface — recorded as programme dual for far U

consequence.zero_free_path_segments: Away from zeros / in ZF region near sigma=1, classical |zeta'/zeta| bounds give far U << (log^2|t|)/log X — may be small; does not cover approach-to-zero arcs

barrier.name: Zero-Entangled Frequency Barrier (ZEFB)
barrier.statement: The frequency gamma* is not a free Diophantine parameter; it is the ordinate of a zero of zeta. Large-value questions for sum Lambda(n) n^{-rho*} are entangled with the vanishing of the Euler product / zeta at rho*. Almost-all gamma metric theorems do not transfer to zero ordinates.

what_was_checked: Generic equidistribution heuristics — insufficient for zero ordinates
Partial sum of p^{-rho*} vs log zeta / zeta' — singular at zeros
No metric theorem found that forces limsup |S_X(rho*)|=infinity at a zero

resolution.relation_to_FFML: ZEFB is the arithmetic dual of FFML: FFML blocks free-t methods; ZEFB blocks treating gamma* as a generic Diophantine frequency

MA6_Diophantine.conclusion: MA6 does not yield Form C. Named ZEFB: zero-entangled frequency blocks generic Diophantine transfer. FFML+ZEFB together fence free-t and generic-n Diophantine attacks.
